rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape [16, 16384] → size = 262144. The kernel selection condition is `if (size >= 4096 && (size % 4) == 0)`. Since 262144 >= 4096 (TRUE) AND 262144 % 4 == 0 (TRUE), the condition is TRUE, so `elu_kernel_vectorized4` is always called. The mutated `elu_kernel_fast` kernel (where line 24 changes blockDim.x→blockDim.y) is in the else branch and is NEVER executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `blockDim.x` to `blockDim.y` on line 24 of the `elu_kernel_fast` kernel, which would change the stride from `256 * gridDim.x` to `1 * gridDim.x` (since 1D blocks have blockDim.y=1 implicitly). However, this kernel is only called when `size < 4096 || size % 4 != 0`. With the fixed input shape [16, 16384], the total element count is 262144, which satisfies `size >= 4096 && size % 4 == 0`, causing the code to always use `elu_kernel_vectorized4` instead. The mutated kernel is therefore dead code under the fixed-shape contract and cannot be exercised by any value-level test.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutated code path (`elu_kernel_fast`) is only reachable when input has <4096 elements or non-multiple-of-4 element count. With fixed shape [16, 16384] = 262144 elements (≥4096 and divisible by 4), the vectorized kernel is always used. Killing this mutant requires changing input shapes, which violates the contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should track code path coverage per kernel. When multiple kernel variants exist (e.g., fast vs vectorized), ensure test inputs exercise ALL code paths. Consider adding a test with shape yielding size < 4096 or size % 4 != 0 to cover the `elu_kernel_fast` branch in future testing contracts.
